title.narrative: Strengthening the Social Contract through Socio-Economic Infrastructure

description.narrative: The proposed Overall Objective for the action is: Strengthened legitimacy of government authorities in selected underserved communities, through integrated climate-adaptive infrastructure, sustainable livelihoods and social contract-strengthening initiatives. In recent years, there have been significant efforts to reclaim territory from al-Shabaab in Somalia, with the Somali government and its partners achieving substantial gains. Since August 2022, the UN reported that over 600 kilometers of ground had been liberated from the group. These liberated areas face significant challenges, including environmental degradation, natural resource depletion, and limited access to basic services and sustainable livelihoods. This Action seeks to build on existing successful mechanisms that were established through previous projects and to ensure these immediate gains are transformed into a sustainable social contract between the communities and the government (at federal, regional, and local level). In that respect the action will focus on three specific objectives that can contribute to rebuild trust and increase economic development for the targeted communities:1. Socio-economic infrastructure: Reconciliation and trust between citizens and government institutions are rebuilt in recovered areas following the (re-)establishment of socio-economic infrastructure and furnishing/equipping existing public infrastructure. The selection of local infrastructure such as markets or townhalls will be decided together with the communities and with the direct participation of the communities. The direct implication of communities in infrastructure projects, for instance through cofinancing mechanisms, has proven to strengthen social cohesion and increase ownership of the project.2. Climate-adaptive livelihoods: With 83% of the population employed in agriculture, improving livelihood in rural areas will only be done through better resource management and improved agricultural / pastoral practices. The objective of the action is to replicate existing mechanisms of community ressources management in ways that restore ecosystems, enhance climate resilience, and create sustainable economic opportunities. There are multiple examples where nature-based and regenerative solutions combined with inclusive governance structures ensure  environmental sustainability, peacebuilding, and economic resilience. This will also improve community resilience to climate change and reduce conflict over the access to natural resources.3. Social contract strengthening and conflict-sensitivity governance for sustainable peace: Women face challenges in fully participating in peacebuilding efforts due to a patriarchal society where men traditionally hold power and decision-making authority. However, thanks to various initiatives there is a growing momentum for women's leadership in Somalia's peace efforts.  Women are increasingly recognised for their vital roles in peace and security, particularly in mediating conflicts, bridging clan divisions, and influencing elders.This action will capitalise on past successful experience where women¿s leadership network allowed to address conflict, enhance livelihoods and promote sustainable environmental and natural resources management.The intervention will apply an area-based approach, seeking synergies between social cohesion, livelihoods, and value chain components. This will increase value for money and develop graduation pathways.
